summary: The supplied C++ model is a whole-burst FIFO: multi_test.cpp has one ordered mem_q, only mem_q.front() is served, and the only ID-based reorder is a window-only DS promotion. This means a long completion R burst at the head starves later PTW/DS R beats even when the AXI IDs differ. AXI itself allows beat-boundary interleaving across different IDs while requiring same-ID order. The proposed opt-in +memory-r-interleave=1 patch is C++-model-only: it rotates the next ready distinct AXI ID to the head only when no R payload is held, considers only the oldest outstanding AR per ID, and leaves +memory-r-interleave=0 as the existing FIFO. It does not change RTL, source skid, permission gates, setup-latency fixtures, B/READY fixtures, write counts, or expected data. Strong-variable quantum256 exactly duplicates the prior §51 candidate for all four source trace pairs; no shared-read/broadcast/group-drop/translate-first novelty is claimed here.

evidence.claim: Hybrid IOMMU signals TLB miss back to the master and drops the transaction.
evidence.support: Negative-fault/no-buffer scope: the missing transaction is not absorbed in an IOMMU data buffer; it is reported back and dropped so the source can retry later.

evidence.claim: On a TLB miss the IOMMU stores metadata in a hardware queue, responds with an error, drops the transaction, and processes the next one.
evidence.support: Exact negative-fault outcome and no-data-buffer scope for the 2018 hybrid IOMMU.

evidence.claim: Conventional DMA burst transfers to SVM traditionally need buffers to absorb TLB-missing write bursts; such buffers are overprovisioned and stall all SVM accesses once full.
evidence.support: Establishes the problem scope the 2018 paper avoids: no additional data buffer and no global stall.

evidence.claim: The paper adds lightweight hardware to a standard DMA engine to detect and react to TLB misses, supporting parallel burst DMA to SVM without additional buffers.
evidence.support: Confirms the no-buffer, per-burst miss-detection design point.

evidence.claim: An AXI burst may not cross a page, so each burst requires exactly one TLB entry at the instant its request arrives at the IOMMU; consecutive bursts can arrive back-to-back and only need entries briefly.
evidence.support: This is request-time per-burst translation, not whole-transfer destination preflight.

evidence.claim: The retirement buffer tracks in-flight bursts and must keep same-ID order while allowing different AXI IDs to complete in any order; therefore it cannot be a simple FIFO, and one FIFO per AXI ID would waste hardware.
evidence.support: Direct evidence that AXI ordering is per-ID, not whole-burst FIFO across IDs.

evidence.claim: The retirement buffer stores only metadata (32-bit virtual start, 16-bit local start, 3-bit ID, 8-bit length, 3-bit status; under 8 B per burst), requiring 64 B for the same miss tolerance as a 16 KiB data buffer.
evidence.support: Quantifies the no-data-buffer claim.

evidence.claim: ShareMMU's transient state drains in-flight memory requests: after the accelerator drains, the host receives flush acknowledgment, the PT entry is evicted or permissions are updated, and the shared TLB is unlocked. The protocol is deadlock-free because stalled TLB misses wait passively at the locked shared TLB and do not consume accelerator execution resources, while in-flight TLB hits complete in bounded time because physical-memory permissions remain valid until the host commits.
evidence.support: This is the drain/deadlock premise that must be compared against the current streaming-DMA model.

evidence.claim: When an address is invalidated, the accelerator must flush that entry, the per-accelerator permission bit is cleared to no-access, and the next access triggers a translation miss and a page-table walk that retrieves updated permissions.
evidence.support: Permission propagation path after revocation.

evidence.claim: If an accelerator refuses to flush its translation on a back-invalidation request, it can never use the stale translation because the translation will not be present in the Permission Tracker.
evidence.support: Denied-request outcome: stale use is blocked by the tracker, not by trusting the accelerator.

evidence.claim: If a request misses the Permission Tracker or has incorrect permissions, it is flagged as a malicious access that needs OS handling.
evidence.support: Explicit denied-request outcome and OS-visible fault path.

evidence.claim: The CVA6 dma_core_wrap instantiates idma_backend with ErrorCap = idma_pkg::NO_ERROR_HANDLING.
evidence.support: Shows the DMA core is not configured for recoverable error handling.

evidence.claim: .idma_eh_req_i is tied to '0 and .eh_req_valid_i is tied to 1'b1, with the comment 'No error handling'.
evidence.support: Confirms no error-handling request path is exercised in this integration.

evidence.claim: The original DMA engine was not designed to deal with error responses recoverably and reported a transfer as complete as soon as it received the final read or write response of the last burst, regardless of whether all bursts succeeded.
evidence.support: Explains why NO_ERROR_HANDLING affects testing: a denied/error response can be treated as completion unless the DMA is extended.

evidence.claim: The behavioural DDR model uses a single ordered R-return queue: std::deque<MemRead> mem_q; // SINGLE ordered R-return queue.
evidence.support: This is the model's whole-burst FIFO ordering point.

evidence.claim: On f_ddr_ar, the harness pushes a MemRead with id, addr, len, beat=0, latency=ptw_latency, and accepted_cycle=g_cycle.
evidence.support: Shows AR acceptance order and per-request age source.

evidence.claim: ddr_ar_ready is asserted only when bp_ready and mem_q.size() < 16.
evidence.support: Defines the bounded shared-DDR AR queue depth.

evidence.claim: drive_ddr() sets RVALID=0, returns if mem_q is empty, optionally promotes one DS request, then serves only mem_q.front(); setup latency and R payload are derived from that front entry.
evidence.support: Proves the default model is whole-burst FIFO across all IDs except the explicit DS promotion.

evidence.claim: The only ID-based reorder is ds_priority: if ds_priority && win_open and the front is not DS, the oldest DS request is rotated to the front. The preceding comment explicitly says AXI allows R interleaving across different IDs.
evidence.support: Distinguishes AXI per-ID semantics from the model's FIFO implementation and identifies the only existing exception.

evidence.claim: On an R handshake, only mem_q.front() is advanced or popped: if beat == len, mem_q.pop_front(); else h.beat++.
evidence.support: Confirms no other queued request can receive R beats while the front is outstanding.

evidence.claim: s_ddr_r_held is top->ddr_r_valid && !top->ddr_r_ready, and ddr_r_held is updated from it at the rising edge; drive_ddr() uses !ddr_r_held to skip rotations.
evidence.support: This is the existing first-VALID R payload stability guard.

evidence.claim: top->ddr_r_id is driven from mem_q.front().id and echoed verbatim as the 6-bit shared-DDR ID.
evidence.support: ID is carried per request and must remain stable with the payload.

evidence.claim: The natural trace emits rfirst when h.beat == 0 and rlast when h.beat == h.len, using mem_q.front() before pop.
evidence.support: Under interleave, rfirst/rlast and per-region Rcount remain tied to the actual request whose beat is served.

evidence.claim: Only the completion master (crossbar slave port 2, i.e. (id>>4)&3 == 2) carries DMA payload; DS/PTW walks, debug, and synthetic CPU are excluded.
evidence.support: Identifies the long data R stream whose head-of-line blocking can starve PTW/DS R.

evidence.claim: The harness prints: 'ptw latency is a plain model delay (DDL/DDR), NOT MIG-matched.'
evidence.support: No physical MIG result is claimed; all ordering/latency evidence is from this behavioural model.

prior_boundaries: No RTL change is proposed here. The patch is only for out/shared-read-frontier-20261009/multi_test.cpp.
No source skid, permission gate, IOMMU translation-controller, or DMA core change is proposed here; the root must make those separately.
Strong-variable quantum256 is exactly the prior §51 candidate for all four source trace pairs and is not re-sold as new.
Shared read, broadcast, group drop, and translate-first are prior §50/§51 material and are not claimed as new.
The proposal does not claim board timing, MIG-matched latency, or physical DDR behaviour. It is a C++ testbench model change only.
The default +memory-r-interleave=0 must remain exactly the existing whole-burst FIFO mem_q model.
assumptions: The supplied line numbers correspond to the actual compiled out/shared-read-frontier-20261009/multi_test.cpp.
The new flag +memory-r-interleave=0|1 is test-only, default 0, and is not written into any DUT register.

Interleave mode uses per-request readiness g_cycle > accepted_cycle + ptw_latency, matching the existing +read-latency-model=overlap condition. The serial countdown path is unchanged when +memory-r-interleave=0.
Only the oldest outstanding AR for a given AXI ID is eligible for selection, so same-ID AR order is preserved.

The existing ddr_r_held guard prevents rotation while an R beat is offered and not accepted, preserving first-VALID payload stability. This relies on the existing model invariant and does not add a new DDR R payload shadow.
When +ds-priority=1 and a DS request is promoted this cycle, interleave selection is skipped for that cycle, preserving the existing DS-priority behaviour.
The patch does not add or rename any JSON field and does not change +memory-b-delay, +memory-backpressure, write_tail_pause, write counts, or expected byte checks.
Root reviews the concurrency-critical RTL source before applying any corresponding RTL change; this C++ patch is not a substitute for that review.
No command was executed and no test result is claimed. All acceptance checks below are proposed verification steps.

acceptance_checks: Default invariance: run the existing natural shared-source case with +memory-r-interleave=0. Require exit 0, PASS, all byte checks and terminal checks unchanged, and byte-for-byte identical sample.trace rfirst/rlast/Rcount and region totals versus the pre-patch run.
Opt-in completion: run the same case with +memory-r-interleave=1. Require exit 0, PASS, all existing byte checks, write counts, expected-data checks, and terminal JSON checks unchanged.
Same-ID order: parse sample.trace and, for each AXI ID, verify no later rfirst for that ID appears before the earlier rlast for the same ID. This must hold under +memory-r-interleave=1.

Distinct-ID interleave evidence: under +memory-r-interleave=1, verify at least one rfirst for ID X occurs before an rlast for a different ID Y (X != Y) when multiple IDs and long bursts are present. This proves beat-boundary interleave rather than whole-burst FIFO.

rfirst/rlast/Rcount preservation: under +memory-r-interleave=1, verify per-region rfirst count, rlast count, and R beat count match the +memory-r-interleave=0 run. Interleaving may change order, not totals.

Held-payload stability: run +memory-r-interleave=1 with +memory-backpressure=1 to force RVALID&&!RREADY episodes. The existing ddr_r_held guard must prevent any rotation while a beat is held. If a stronger check is required, add a DDR R payload shadow; the current file has only read-admission AR stability shadows, so this observable is missing today.

DS-priority compatibility: if +ds-priority=1 is used, verify the existing DS-priority behaviour is preserved when a DS request is promoted, and that interleave does not override that promotion in the same cycle.

No fixture drift: verify the patch does not alter +ptw-latency, +memory-b-delay, +memory-backpressure, write_tail_pause, write counts, expected data, or any existing JSON schema field. Only +memory-r-interleave is added.
